column1: # Curated nutrition for local Malaysian dishes, per 100g of the dish as served.
# Why this file exists: USDA's search covers American foods and generic
# ingredients, and has no entry for any composite Malaysian dish. Asked about
# one it still answers — a benchmark of 30 local dishes had 26% of its USDA
# matches come back arithmetically impossible ("nasi lemak" resolved to plain
# chicken with 0g carbohydrate; "black pepper chicken chop rice" to the spice
# itself). This table is consulted first so recognised dishes never reach that
# lookup, and USDA is left to do what it is actually good at: single ingredients.
# Values are curated approximations assembled from published Malaysian serving
# figures and typical stall portions, intended for ranking dishes against one
# another rather than for clinical use. Macros reconcile with the stated energy
# at 4/4/9 to within a few percent.
# Matching is case-insensitive on the longest alias contained in the dish name,
# so a more specific row always beats a more general one.
